title: How the Moon affects us
titleChinese: 月亮变化会影响人类行为吗？
paragraphs: It’s more than 384,000km from Earth. We can see it most nights. And it’s not made of cheese! I am, of course, talking about the Moon. Astronauts have taken giant steps to explore this natural satellite floating in space, but despite it being out of reach for most of us, it still moves us in mysterious ways.

The Moon, obviously, provides moonlight. A full moon, seen roughly once a month, can light up our way on an otherwise dark night. But while this lunar light can be impressive to look at, it can affect our sleeping patterns. One study showed that during or around the full moon, those studied spent less time in deep sleep, slept for less time and reported having poorer sleep, despite sleeping in a dark room not exposed to moonlight.

There are many theories about how the Moon can affect other things too. One study suggested animals are more likely to bite us during a full moon. And many moons ago, it was thought the Moon induced lunacy – the word derives from the Latin word ‘lunaticus’, meaning ‘moonstruck’, and evolved from the idea that celestial changes could cause periods of insanity. Even winemakers look to the Moon when planting and pruning grapevines. They will avoid a full moon at all costs because, although the added moisture in the soil at this time may give a fuller and juicier grape, the additional water is thought to dilute the taste of the fruit, which results in a less successful vintage.

The Moon might affect our behaviour too. Writing about this for BBC Future, Claudia Hammond explains one interesting theory. Just as the Moon’s gravitational pull affects the tides, it exerts its influence on the water in our bodies. But she points out “the Moon is smaller than the Earth, so its gravitational pull is correspondingly less powerful. What’s more, it exerts the same force on us regardless of whether it’s new or full.” Research into ancient myths about the effects of the lunar cycle on us is ongoing. So, like the Moon being made of cheese, we must be careful what we believe!

vocabulary.entry: natural satellite /ˈnætʃrəl ˈsætəlaɪt/ 天然卫星
vocabulary.example: The Moon is Earth’s only natural satellite.
vocabulary.translation: 月球是地球唯一的天然卫星。

vocabulary.entry: float in space /fləʊt ɪn speɪs/ 漂浮在太空中
vocabulary.example: Astronomers observed a small asteroid floating in space near the Earth.
vocabulary.translation: 天文学家观测到一颗小行星漂浮在地球附近的太空中。

vocabulary.entry: out of reach /ˌaʊt əv ˈriːtʃ/ 遥不可及；无法触及
vocabulary.example: The top of the shelf is out of reach for the little girl.
vocabulary.translation: 这个小女孩够不着架子的顶端。

vocabulary.entry: move sb in mysterious ways /muːv ˈsʌmbədi ɪn mɪˈstɪəriəs weɪz/ 以神秘的方式影响某人
vocabulary.example: Nature moves us in mysterious ways that we cannot fully explain.
vocabulary.translation: 大自然以我们无法完全解释的神秘方式影响着我们。

vocabulary.entry: moonlight /ˈmuːnlaɪt/ n. 月光
vocabulary.example: We walked along the beach under the soft moonlight.
vocabulary.translation: 我们在柔和的月光下沿着海滩散步。

vocabulary.entry: full moon /fʊl muːn/ 满月
vocabulary.example: They held a party in the garden during the full moon.
vocabulary.translation: 他们在满月时于花园里举办了一场派对。

vocabulary.entry: lunar /ˈluːnə(r)/ adj. 月球的；与月亮相关的
vocabulary.example: The lunar eclipse will be visible in most parts of the country tonight.
vocabulary.translation: 今晚全国大部分地区都能观测到月食。

vocabulary.entry: sleeping pattern /ˈsliːpɪŋ ˈpætn/ 睡眠规律
vocabulary.example: Jet lag can disrupt your sleeping pattern for several days.
vocabulary.translation: 时差会让你的睡眠规律紊乱好几天。

vocabulary.entry: expose to /ɪkˈspəʊz tuː/ 暴露于；使接触
vocabulary.example: Don’t expose your skin to strong sunlight for too long.
vocabulary.translation: 不要让你的皮肤长时间暴露在强烈的阳光下。

vocabulary.entry: many moons ago /ˈmeni muːnz əˈɡəʊ/ 很久以前
vocabulary.example: Many moons ago, people used to hunt animals for food and clothing.
vocabulary.translation: 很久以前，人们靠狩猎动物获取食物和衣物。

vocabulary.entry: induce /ɪnˈdjuːs/ v. 诱发；引起
vocabulary.example: The medicine may induce drowsiness in some patients.
vocabulary.translation: 这种药可能会使部分患者产生困倦感。

vocabulary.entry: lunacy /ˈluːnəsi/ n. 精神失常；荒唐行为
vocabulary.example: Some people thought his decision to quit his job was sheer lunacy.
vocabulary.translation: 有些人认为他辞职的决定完全是荒唐之举。

vocabulary.entry: derive from /dɪˈraɪv frəm/ 源自；起源于
vocabulary.example: This word derives from a Greek term meaning “love of wisdom”.
vocabulary.translation: 这个词源自希腊语，意为“爱智慧”。

vocabulary.entry: Latin /ˈlætɪn/ n. 拉丁语
vocabulary.example: Many scientific and legal terms come from Latin.
vocabulary.translation: 许多科学和法律术语都来源于拉丁语。

vocabulary.entry: moonstruck /ˈmuːnstrʌk/ adj. 受月亮影响的；精神恍惚的
vocabulary.example: The poet was said to be moonstruck and wrote many romantic poems.
vocabulary.translation: 据说这位诗人有些痴狂，创作了许多浪漫的诗歌。

vocabulary.entry: celestial /səˈlestɪəl/ adj. 天体的；天空的
vocabulary.example: Astronomers study celestial bodies such as stars and planets.
vocabulary.translation: 天文学家研究恒星、行星等天体。

vocabulary.entry: insanity /ɪnˈsænəti/ n. 精神错乱；疯狂
vocabulary.example: The pressure of the job drove him to the brink of insanity.
vocabulary.translation: 工作压力把他逼到了精神崩溃的边缘。

vocabulary.entry: winemaker /ˈwaɪnmeɪkə(r)/ n. 酿酒师
vocabulary.example: The winemaker has over 30 years of experience in producing red wine.
vocabulary.translation: 这位酿酒师有超过三十年的红酒酿造经验。

vocabulary.entry: prune /pruːn/ v. 修剪（树木、灌木等）
vocabulary.example: You should prune the roses in winter to promote better growth.
vocabulary.translation: 你应该在冬天修剪玫瑰，以促进其更好地生长。

vocabulary.entry: grapevine /ˈɡreɪpvaɪn/ n. 葡萄藤
vocabulary.example: 秋天时，葡萄园里的葡萄藤挂满了果实。
vocabulary.translation: The grapevines in the vineyard are heavy with fruit in autumn.

vocabulary.entry: avoid...at all costs /əˈvɔɪd æt ɔːl kɒsts/ 不惜一切代价避免
vocabulary.example: We must avoid a repeat of the disaster at all costs.
vocabulary.translation: 我们必须不惜一切代价避免灾难再次发生。

vocabulary.entry: moisture /ˈmɔɪstʃə(r)/ n. 水分；湿气
vocabulary.example: The plants need more moisture during the dry season.
vocabulary.translation: 干旱季节里，这些植物需要更多的水分。

vocabulary.entry: dilute /daɪˈluːt/ v. 稀释；冲淡
vocabulary.example: She diluted the concentrated juice with water before drinking.
vocabulary.translation: 她喝水前把浓缩果汁用水稀释了。

vocabulary.entry: vintage /ˈvɪntɪdʒ/ n. 特定年份酿造的葡萄酒；佳酿
vocabulary.example: This 2018 vintage is one of the best wines from the region.
vocabulary.translation: 这款2018年份的葡萄酒是该产区最好的佳酿之一。

vocabulary.entry: gravitational pull /ˌɡrævɪˈteɪʃənl pʊl/ 引力
vocabulary.example: The Earth’s gravitational pull keeps the Moon in its orbit.
vocabulary.translation: 地球引力使月球保持在其轨道上运行。

vocabulary.entry: tide /taɪd/ n. 潮汐；潮水
vocabulary.example: The tide is going out, and we can see many shells on the beach.
vocabulary.translation: 潮水正在退去，我们能在沙滩上看到很多贝壳。

vocabulary.entry: exert influence on /ɪɡˈzɜːt ˈɪnfluəns ɒn/ 对……施加影响
vocabulary.example: Parents exert a great influence on their children’s character.
vocabulary.translation: 父母对孩子的性格有着极大的影响。

vocabulary.entry: correspondingly /ˌkɒrəˈspɒndɪŋli/ adv. 相应地；对应地
vocabulary.example: As the demand increases, prices will rise correspondingly.
vocabulary.translation: 随着需求的增加，价格也会相应上涨。

vocabulary.entry: lunar cycle /ˈluːnə(r) ˈsaɪkl/ 月相周期
vocabulary.example: The lunar cycle lasts about 29.5 days from one new moon to the next.
vocabulary.translation: 月相周期从一次新月到下一次新月大约持续29.5天。

vocabulary.entry: ongoing /ˈɒnɡəʊɪŋ/ adj. 进行中的；持续的
vocabulary.example: The ongoing research aims to find a cure for the rare disease.
vocabulary.translation: 这项正在进行的研究旨在找到治疗这种罕见疾病的方法。

sentences.english: It’s more than 384,000km from Earth. We can see it most nights.
sentences.chinese: 它距离地球超过38.4万公里，我们在大多数夜晚都能看到它，而且它根本不是奶酪做的！

sentences.english: And it’s not made of cheese!
I am, of course, talking about the Moon.
sentences.chinese: 在探索这颗悬浮在太空中的天然卫星的征程中，宇航员们已经取得了巨大进展。

sentences.english: Astronauts have taken giant steps to explore this natural satellite floating in space, but despite it being out of reach for most of us, it still moves us in mysterious ways.
sentences.chinese: 尽管对我们大多数人来说，月球遥不可及，但它仍以神秘的方式影响着我们。

sentences.english: A full moon, seen roughly once a month, can light up our way on an otherwise dark night.
sentences.chinese: 满月大约每月出现一次，它能在漆黑的夜晚照亮我们前行的路。

sentences.english: But while this lunar light can be impressive to look at, it can affect our sleeping patterns.
sentences.chinese: 不过，尽管月色看起来令人赞叹，它却会影响我们的睡眠规律。

sentences.english: One study showed that during or around the full moon, those studied spent less time in deep sleep, slept for less time and reported having poorer sleep, despite sleeping in a dark room not exposed to moonlight.
sentences.chinese: 一项研究表明，在满月期间或前后，即使研究对象身处没有月光照射的黑暗房间里，他们的深度睡眠时间和总睡眠时间也会减少，而且睡眠质量也更差。

sentences.english: There are many theories about how the Moon can affect other things too.
sentences.chinese: 关于月球如何影响其他事物，也存在诸多理论。

sentences.english: One study suggested animals are more likely to bite us during a full moon.
sentences.chinese: 有研究指出，动物在满月期间更容易咬人。

sentences.english: And many moons ago, it was thought the Moon induced lunacy – the word derives from the Latin word ‘lunaticus’, meaning ‘moonstruck’, and evolved from the idea that celestial changes could cause periods of insanity.
sentences.chinese: 很久以前，人们还认为月球会引发精神失常——“lunacy”这个词源自拉丁语“lunaticus”，意为“受月亮影响的”，这个说法源于“天体变化可能导致精神失常发作”的观点。

sentences.english: Even winemakers look to the Moon when planting and pruning grapevines.
sentences.chinese: 就连酿酒师在种植和修剪葡萄藤时也会参照月相。

sentences.english: They will avoid a full moon at all costs because, although the added moisture in the soil at this time may give a fuller and juicier grape, the additional water is thought to dilute the taste of the fruit, which results in a less successful vintage.
sentences.chinese: 他们会不惜一切代价避开满月时段，因为尽管此时土壤中额外的水分能让葡萄长得更饱满多汁，但这些多余的水分会稀释果实的风味，进而酿造出品质欠佳的葡萄酒。

sentences.english: The Moon might affect our behaviour too.
sentences.chinese: 月球或许也会影响人类的行为。

sentences.english: Writing about this for BBC Future, Claudia Hammond explains one interesting theory. Just as the Moon’s gravitational pull affects the tides, it exerts its influence on the water in our bodies.
sentences.chinese: 克劳迪娅·哈蒙德在为BBC未来频道撰写相关文章时，阐释了一个有趣的理论：就像月球引力会影响潮汐一样，它也会对人体中的水分产生作用。

sentences.english: But she points out “the Moon is smaller than the Earth, so its gravitational pull is correspondingly less powerful.
sentences.chinese: 但她也指出：“月球比地球小，所以其引力也相应较弱。

sentences.english: What’s more, it exerts the same force on us regardless of whether it’s new or full.”
sentences.chinese: 此外，无论新月还是满月，月球对人体施加的引力都是相同的。”

sentences.english: Research into ancient myths about the effects of the lunar cycle on us is ongoing.
sentences.chinese: 关于月相周期对人类影响的古老传说，相关研究仍在进行中。

sentences.english: So, like the Moon being made of cheese, we must be careful what we believe!
sentences.chinese: 所以，就像“月球是奶酪做的”这种说法一样，我们对听到的各种观点都应该保持审慎！
